long_biography.plain_text:
Coffee drew Swedish businessman Anders Nordquist away from a planned legal career. While completing his dissertation at Stockholm University, he spent half a day talking with the family company's coffee buyer about beans, plantations and production. He subsequently entered purchasing himself, visiting growers in East Africa and Latin America to taste their coffee and understand their businesses.

His attention also turned to packaging. Coffee had been sold with cardboard, aluminium foil and plastic lids, a combination he considered costly and excessive. The company invested in new machinery and redesigned its packs. It also pursued certification of the coffee beans it purchased.
long_biography.html:
Coffee drew Swedish businessman Anders Nordquist away from a planned legal career. While completing his dissertation at Stockholm University, he spent half a day talking with the family company's coffee buyer about beans, plantations and production. He subsequently entered purchasing himself, visiting growers in East Africa and Latin America to taste their coffee and understand their businesses.

His attention also turned to packaging. Coffee had been sold with cardboard, aluminium foil and plastic lids, a combination he considered costly and excessive. The company invested in new machinery and redesigned its packs. It also pursued certification of the coffee beans it purchased.
